title: Parts of a Flowering Plant
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Parts of a Flowering Plant Worksheets (Roots, Stem, Leaves, Flowers)
standard_text: Identify and describe the functions of different parts of flowering plants: roots, stem/trunk, leaves and flowers.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on the parts of a flowering plant: roots, stem, leaves and flowers, their jobs, a labelled plant and the parts we eat. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Roots drink, stems hold up, leaves make food, flowers make seeds.
body_html:
How to think about it

A flowering plant has four main parts, and each part has a job.

  • Roots take in water and nutrients and hold the plant in the ground.
  • The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves. A tree trunk is a stem.
  • Leaves use sunlight to make food. Flowers make seeds.
Example

Which part takes in water?

It is under the soil

Answer: the roots

Example

When we eat a carrot, which part is it?

It grows down into the soil

Answer: the root

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants get their food from the soil.
  • Thinking a tree trunk is not a stem.
  • Thinking flowers are only there to look pretty.

faq.q: What are the parts of a flowering plant?
faq.a: The main parts are the roots, the stem (a trunk on a tree), the leaves and the flowers.
Roots take in water and hold the plant still. The stem holds it up and carries water. Leaves make food using sunlight. Flowers make seeds.
No. Plants make their own food in their leaves. They take in water and nutrients from the soil through their roots.
